title: Quarterly dedicated capacity: Autoscales governance, SLO-triggers and initiative task slices
creator: Elena Ruiz
description: This ticket captures the quarter-level plan to align Dedicated capacity autoscale behavior with SLO-driven governance, rollout task slices, and cross-functional owners. Goal: define guardrails and decision criteria so Dedicated pools can scale predictably while minimizing cost and preserving latency SLAs. Outputs: initiative map, phased task slices for engineering/design/ops, runbook triggers for SLO crossings, and a small scoreboard of leading indicators.
acceptance_criteria: Roadmap doc with initiative map and priority slices published to Confluence
Runbook draft that defines three SLO-trigger levels and automated actions (notify, prewarm, scale) reviewed by infra and SRE
Cross-team owners assigned for each task slice with estimates and clear handoffs
Telemetry dashboard with leading indicators (queue length, tail latency, reserve occupancy) linked in ticket
Canary plan for phased rollout with rollback criteria and cost guardrails
comments: 2026-01-04 - Elena Ruiz: Kickoff with SRE, infra and product. Agreed to target three trigger tiers: WATCH, PREWARM, FULL-BURST. Action: Marcus to draft trigger definitions.
2026-01-08 - Marcus Lee: First pass of trigger thresholds posted. Need validation against historical traffic; assigned ENG-20456 for simulation runs.

2026-01-11 - Priya Nair (SRE): Simulation results show PREWARM threshold at 65% queue occupancy leads to 12% cost increase but avoids SLO breaches in 87% of spikes. Suggest adjusting PREWARM buffer to 60% and adding short-term KV cache warm-up.
2026-01-13 - Design review (Aisha Patel): UX for operator console needs explicit rollback button and explanation of cost impact. Creating small mockups for the rollout canary flow.

2026-01-15 - Marcus Lee: Split work into three task slices (Baseline telemetry, Trigger automation, Operator UX). Created sub-issues: PM-29178, PM-29179, PM-29180. Requesting estimates from infra (ENG) this week.
2026-01-18 - Elena Ruiz: Asked Finance for cost guardrail thresholds; Finance recommended soft limit notifications at estimated +10% and hard rollback at +25%.
2026-01-20 - Marcus Lee: Updated acceptance criteria to include telemetry dashboard link and canary rollback criteria. Preparing canary runbook stub for ops rehearsal in Cycle 6.
decision_log: Decision 2026-01-04: Use three-tier trigger model (WATCH / PREWARM / FULL-BURST) to balance latency vs cost.
Decision 2026-01-11: PREWARM buffer reduced from 65% to 60% after cost/benefit simulation.
Decision 2026-01-18: Finance soft/hard guardrail thresholds accepted (+10% notify, +25% auto-rollback).
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Over-eager PREWARM causing sustained cost increases. Mitigation: implement decay timer to revert PREWARM after sustained low utilization and use queued-request smoothing.
Risk: False positives from bursty small customers triggering scale. Mitigation: add request-pattern classifier and customer-impact whitelist for critical tenants.
Risk: Rollback flapping. Mitigation: require 3 consecutive violation windows before hard rollback and add manual approval path for enterprise customers.
